September in Seoul

Monthly

5 slides · 1080×1350 (4:5) · @goodlugg · W3_SeptemberSeoul_EN/

Scroll the strip sideways, the way the carousel swipes

Caption

September might be the best month to be in Seoul. 🍂 Summer's humidity finally breaks. The July–August crowds have gone home. And the light in the late afternoon is the reason people keep coming back. What to expect: · Warm afternoons, around 26°C · Evenings down to the high teens — bring one layer · Humidity breaks around mid-month · Chuseok, Korea's harvest holiday, lands late in the month Pack for two seasons in one day. Short sleeves at Gyeongbokgung at 2 PM, a jacket on Namsan at 8. Layers, not bulk — you'll walk further than you planned. Three worth the trip this month: Bukchon Hanok Village, finally walkable without the heat. Seoul Forest, for that late-September light. Namsan at sunset, when the sky is clear enough to see all of it. And if September takes you further than Seoul — Goodlugg moves your bags to the next city the same day, so the itinerary doesn't have to bend around a suitcase. goodlugg.com 💜 Where are you headed this month? 👇 #SeoulTravel #TravelKorea #KoreaTravel #VisitKorea #SeoulInSeptember #KoreaTrip #SeoulAutumn #Chuseok #BukchonHanokVillage #Namsan #SeoulForest #TravelLight #HandsFreeTravel #LuggageDelivery #Goodlugg #KoreaTravelTips #KoreaItinerary #AutumnInKorea

4 Days, 2 Cities

Travel plan

5 slides · 1080×1350 (4:5) · @goodlugg · W4_Itinerary_EN/

Scroll the strip sideways, the way the carousel swipes

Caption

Every Korea itinerary online is written as if you're travelling empty-handed. 🧳 Here's a 4-day, 2-city route that actually accounts for the suitcase. DAY 1 · SEOUL Land at Incheon and send your bags straight to your Seoul hotel. Gyeongbokgung and Bukchon on foot, jet lag and all. Dinner in Euljiro — the bags beat you to the room. DAY 2 · SEOUL → BUSAN This is the day every other itinerary gets wrong. Your bags leave the Seoul hotel in the morning. You take the KTX at noon with a daypack. They're at your Busan hotel before dinner. DAY 3–4 · BUSAN Gamcheon, Haeundae, Jagalchi Market. Out of the room at 11, flight much later — so send the bags ahead and spend the gap at the beach instead of a locker room. Two cities in four days is only easy if your suitcase isn't part of the plan. Three decisions we need

None of these block making more content — they block posting it. Each one is a five-minute answer from someone who already knows it.

How often, starting when?

The brief is one post a week, continuously. Five are ready, which covers five weeks. Pick a posting day and we build ahead of it rather than scrambling each week — every format here is repeatable with a new subject.

Marketing

Confirm the locations we name

The posts name hotels, Airbnbs, KTX stations and airports as places bags can be collected. Someone on product should confirm each one is currently bookable before these publish, so the copy matches what a reader actually finds.

Product

Are we cleared to state prices?

Not one post mentions a price, deliberately. If we're cleared to publish per-bag pricing and the same-day cut-off time, these posts get noticeably more persuasive.
